system: English common law and local statutes

constitution.history: several previous; latest approved 10 June 2009, entered into force 6 November 2009 (The Cayman Islands Constitution Order 2009)

courts.highest: Court of Appeal (consists of the court president and at least 2 judges); Grand Court (consists of the court president and at least 2 judges)
courts.judges: Court of Appeal and Grand Court judges appointed by the governor on the advice of the Judicial and Legal Services Commission, an 8-member independent body consisting of governor appointees, Court of Appeal president, and attorneys; Court of Appeal judges' tenure based on their individual instruments of appointment; Grand Court judges normally appointed until retirement at age 65 but can be extended until age 70
courts.note: appeals beyond the Court of Appeal are heard by the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council (in London)

gov.type: parliamentary democracy; self-governing overseas territory of the UK

executive.chosen: the monarchy is hereditary; governor appointed by the monarch; following legislative elections, the governor appoints the leader of the majority party or majority coalition as premier
executive.cabinet: Cabinet selected from the Parliament and appointed by the governor on the advice of the premier

b: The Cayman Islands is a British Overseas Territory and has its own laws.
Religion and family are of significant cultural importance across the Cayman Islands. Many shops, banks and services close on Sundays.
There are harsh penalties for those caught with drugs of any kind. Penalties can include imprisonment for up to 35 years, and fines of unlimited amounts.

Same-sex civil partnerships were legalised in 2020. Hotels and resorts are generally welcoming, regardless of sexual orientation. Local attitudes can be conservative and some people may not approve of same-sex couples showing affection in public.
